title: Migration planning, mapping, rehearsal, reconciliation, and rollback
objectives: Plan a record migration as sequenced loads (parents before children) with External IDs, not as a single unmapped CSV.
Treat field mapping as the contract that decides which columns land; unmapped Wizard fields are not imported.
Rehearse in a sandbox whose data shape you understand; Developer sandboxes may copy little or no record data.
Reconcile with counts and success/error files, and describe rollback as restore/undelete/reverse load—not a platform Undo Migration button.
diagnostic_question: You must move LAB_ Accounts and Contacts from a legacy org into a sandbox, then production. What belongs in the migration plan, the mapping sheet, the rehearsal, the reconciliation, and the rollback—and what would you refuse to do first in production?
definition: A data migration is a planned movement of business records: you sequence objects, map source columns to Salesforce fields, rehearse in a sandbox, reconcile counts and errors, and know how you would roll back. The Data Import Wizard and Data Loader are mapping-and-load tools, not a one-click migrate. Sandboxes isolate rehearsal from production. Backup and Recycle Bin restore are the realistic rollback paths. ([Import Data with the Data Import Wizard](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.import_with_data_import_wizard.htm); [When to Use a Sandbox](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.deploy_sandboxes_intro.htm); [Best practices to back up Salesforce data](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000334121))
why_it_matters: Unrehearsed production loads create duplicates, broken lookups, and no way home. Interviewers listen for parent-before-child, External ID upsert, mapping evidence, sandbox limits, and honest rollback (a copy, not folklore). Deploying metadata is not migrating records.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of an orchestra's opening night. Planning is the program order—strings (Accounts) before chorus (Contacts). Mapping is the score: which chair plays which part; unmapped notes never sound. Rehearsal is the dress rehearsal in an empty hall (sandbox), knowing a small hall may have no audience chairs copied. Reconciliation is comparing the recording to the score and the error list. Rollback is canceling opening night and restoring the previous program from the archive—not a magic 'undo concert' switch on the building.
deeper_explanation: Planning: list objects, volumes, owners, quality gates (DQM-004), identity keys (DQM-003), and load verbs (DQM-002). Sequence parents before children. SOAP create() guidance for parent-then-child in one call still requires the parent first in the array when using External IDs as foreign keys. Org-to-org moves are customer-owned loads, not a hidden Salesforce 'copy all records' button—confirm the current migrate-org knowledge article in the org's Help. Tool choice remains Wizard versus Data Loader versus API/ETL (DQM-001).

Mapping: Wizard Help starts with prepare your data, then map fields; unmapped fields are not imported. Data Loader drag-and-drop maps persist for CLI reuse. A mapping workbook is project metadata you keep in the ticket; it is not a Salesforce object. If a target field does not exist, that is a metadata deploy first (shape), then a data load (instances).

Rehearsal: sandboxes are isolated copies for development, testing, and training without compromising production. Developer and Developer Pro refreshes copy configuration and only a small sample of records—or none of the business records you expected. Do not rehearse a million-row migration only in a Developer sandbox and call it proven. Full/Partial copies are the rehearsal halls that can hold production-like volume when licensed. ([When to Use a Sandbox](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.deploy_sandboxes_intro.htm); [What Data Is Copied to a Developer sandbox](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000387141))

Reconciliation and rollback: success/error CSVs, wizard job metrics, and row-count plus spot-check queries are the evidence. Help: back up before a major data project; restore order preserves relationships. Recycle Bin/undelete restores deletes, not overwrites. SOAP AllOrNoneHeader can roll back one API call if any row fails—it is not a multi-day migration undo. There is no official 'rollback migration' product assumed here; you reverse with delete/undelete, upsert of the pre-image, or a backup product restore.

mental_model.analogy: An orchestra opening night: plan = program order, mapping = the score, rehearsal = dress rehearsal in a sandbox hall, reconciliation = recording versus score, rollback = restore the previous program from the archive—not a building-wide undo switch.
useful_mapping: Migration plan → printed program (object order, volumes, owners)
External ID → each musician's union number that survives venue changes
Field mapping → the score (unmapped notes never play)
Sandbox rehearsal → dress rehearsal in an isolated hall
Developer sandbox → a tiny hall that may have no audience chairs (records)
Success/error CSV → the recording engineer's take sheet
Reconciliation → compare recording to score and attendance counts
Backup extract → archive of last night's performance
AllOrNoneHeader → stop this one take if any chair misses
Production load → opening night after the dress rehearsal passes
where_it_breaks: AllOrNoneHeader is one API call, not the whole season.
A Developer sandbox may not contain the 'audience' (records) you assumed.
Metadata deploy is rebuilding the hall, not seating the audience.
There is no official Undo Concert button on production.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I plan object order and External IDs, map every column, rehearse in a sandbox that can hold the volume, reconcile counts and error files, and roll back from a backup or the Recycle Bin. There is no Undo Migration button. Metadata deploy is not the data move.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: Plan: parents first, keys, verbs, quality gates. Mapping: Wizard unmapped columns never land; Loader maps are artifacts. Rehearsal: sandboxes isolate; Developer sandboxes often lack business records. Reconciliation: success/error CSVs plus queries, not a green bar. Rollback: AllOrNone is one call; deletes may undelete; overwrites need the pre-image. I refuse opening night without a dress rehearsal and a copy of the current production score.

terminology.plain: The written order of objects, keys, volumes, owners, and quality gates before anyone loads.
terminology.precise: A plan names source, target, match keys (External ID), load verb, parent-before-child sequence, rehearsal org, backup, and rollback. It is not a CSV dropped on production.
terminology.example: LAB_ Account upsert, then Contact upsert with Account External ID as the parent key.
terminology.non_example: A single combined CSV with mixed objects and no keys.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Metadata deployment plan: moving fields and validation, not rows.
terminology.boundary: Change-set/DevOps topics own metadata promotion mechanics.

terminology.plain: Which source column becomes which Salesforce field.
terminology.precise: Wizard maps automatically where it can; you must map the rest or those columns never import. Data Loader stores drag-and-drop maps. Missing target fields are a metadata gap first.
terminology.non_example: Hoping Name mapping replaces an External ID.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Matching rule field mapping (DQM-003): how twins compare, not how a CSV lands.
terminology.boundary: Transformation beyond column rename is ETL (DQM-001).

terminology.plain: Running the real mapping and volumes in a sandbox before production.
terminology.precise: Sandboxes isolate testing from production. Developer/Developer Pro may not contain the business records you need; do not call that a volume rehearsal.
terminology.example: Upsert 10,000 LAB_ Accounts in a partial-copy sandbox with the production map.
terminology.non_example: Inserting 5 rows in a Developer sandbox and declaring a 2-million-row job safe.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex test methods: they prove code, not a business-data migration.
terminology.boundary: Data Mask may be required before using production-like PII in a sandbox.

terminology.plain: Proving the target matches the plan: counts, samples, and error files.
terminology.precise: Compare source counts to success CSV counts plus explained errors. Spot-check External IDs and parent lookups. Wizard Recent Import Jobs / Bulk Data Load Jobs are metrics, not the whole proof.
terminology.example: 12,040 source Accounts; 12,031 success; 9 errors documented as missing required fields.
terminology.non_example: A green progress bar with no files kept.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Duplicate job (DQM-003): finds twins, does not prove load completeness.
terminology.boundary: Financial-grade hash reconciliation is a project standard, not a Salesforce object.

terminology.plain: How you put the target back if the load is wrong.
terminology.precise: No assumed Undo Migration product. Paths: AllOrNoneHeader on one SOAP call; undelete if you deleted; reload the pre-image from a backup if you overwrote; stop further waves. Restore order still matters.
terminology.example: Keep the pre-load Account extract; upsert it back if Status__c was wrecked.
terminology.non_example: Expecting Salesforce Support to rewind the org with no copy.
terminology.boundary: hard_delete makes Recycle Bin rollback impossible (DQM-002/005).

when_to_use: When you must plan a migration with object order, External IDs, and parent-before-child loads.
When field mapping is the interview topic, including Wizard unmapped columns never landing.
When rehearsal must happen in a sandbox, and you need to say why a Developer sandbox can lie about volume.
When reconciliation needs success/error files and count queries, not a green progress bar.
When rollback must be described as backup restore, undelete, or reverse upsert—not an Undo Migration button.
when_not_to_use: Do not treat a metadata deploy (fields, validation, Flow) as the record migration itself.
Do not rehearse only in a Developer sandbox that copied no business records and call the volume proven.
Do not use AllOrNoneHeader as if it rolled back yesterday's entire multi-object load.
Do not skip mapping and planning because 'we will upsert on Name.'
Do not run the first full rehearsal in production.

decision_table.signal: Target fields or External IDs do not exist yet.
decision_table.choose: Metadata deploy first, then mapping, then load.
decision_table.not: Load now and 'add fields later' while columns vanish as unmapped.
decision_table.why: Mapping needs a target field. Wizard unmapped columns never import.

decision_table.signal: Accounts and Contacts must move and be retry-safe.
decision_table.choose: Plan Account upsert on External ID, then Contact upsert with the Account External ID as parent.
decision_table.not: Insert both as one mixed file on Name.
decision_table.why: Parents before children; upsert matches a custom External ID.

decision_table.signal: Only a Developer sandbox is available and it has almost no records.
decision_table.choose: Use it for mapping/validation rehearsal; do not claim volume sign-off.
decision_table.not: Call five successful rows a million-row dress rehearsal.
decision_table.why: Developer/Developer Pro typically do not copy ordinary business records.

decision_table.signal: Rehearsal error rate is above the gate, or lookups are blank.
decision_table.choose: Fix mapping or source data and re-rehearse; do not go to production.
decision_table.why: Sandboxes exist so production is not the first hall.

decision_table.choose: Stop waves. Undelete if you deleted. Reload the pre-image if you overwrote. Use AllOrNone only as the already-finished per-call behavior.
decision_table.not: Assume an Undo Migration button or Support rewind with no copy.
decision_table.why: Help: you restore from a copy you have; the bin does not store old field values.

interview_questions.question: Walk a Salesforce data migration using planning, mapping, rehearsal, reconciliation, and rollback.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Plan object order and External IDs. Map every column. Rehearse in a sandbox that can hold the volume. Reconcile with files and queries. Roll back from a copy or the Recycle Bin—not an undo button.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I start with shape versus instances: deploy fields first. I sequence parents before children and choose upsert. I keep maps as artifacts. I refuse a Developer-only volume sign-off. I keep success/error CSVs. I take a pre-image before production. If we fail, I stop waves and pick undelete versus pre-image reload. I mention AllOrNone only as per-call.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ Account then Contact upsert in a partial-copy sandbox, then a gated production-like hall.
follow_ups: What if the field is missing?

interview_questions.question: What is field mapping in a migration, officially?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Matching source columns to Salesforce fields. The Wizard maps what it can; unmapped columns never import. Data Loader stores drag-and-drop maps. Transformation beyond rename is ETL.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show a workbook: source header, target API name, type, requiredness, External ID flag. I list intentional unmapped columns. I refuse Name as the upsert key. If the target field is absent, I stop for metadata. I keep the map with the error files for reconciliation.
interview_questions.example: Customer_No → LAB_ERP_Id__c; Notes column intentionally unmapped.

interview_questions.question: A team rehearsed 20 rows in a Developer sandbox and wants to load two million in production tomorrow. Your answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: That rehearsal proved mapping, not volume. Developer sandboxes typically do not copy ordinary business records. I need a hall that can hold production-like volume, plus LDV and automation enabled like production.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite the Developer sandbox copy article. I ask about duplicate rules, validation, and ownership assignment in both orgs. I ask for Bulk API settings and a backup. I will not bless opening night. If they have no full/partial sandbox, I say the risk out loud and shrink the first production wave—I still want a pre-image.
interview_questions.example: 20 LAB_ Accounts succeeded; production has 2 million with active duplicate rules.
tradeoffs: Wave 0 sample in production vs wait for a fuller sandbox
follow_ups: What does a full copy include?

interview_questions.question: How do you reconcile a finished Account upsert wave?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Source count equals success rows plus explained error rows. Spot-check External IDs and a few field values. Keep the files. A green bar is not reconciliation.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I query COUNT and a few Ids. I open error.csv and classify: required, validation, duplicate, mapping. I check we did not insert extras (count should not grow on a rerun). I sample parent lookups before I start children. I store artifacts in the ticket. If gates fail, I do not start the next object.
interview_questions.example: 12,040 source; 12,031 success; 9 missing LastName; rerun upsert stays at 12,031.
tradeoffs: Block the next wave vs accept known errors
follow_ups: What if success file is missing?

interview_questions.question: Design rollback for three failure modes: partial API call, bad delete, bad overwrite.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Partial call: AllOrNoneHeader if we set it. Bad delete: Recycle Bin/undelete. Bad overwrite: reload the pre-image from the backup we took. None of these is a season-wide undo button.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I write the mode in the plan before we load. I refuse hard_delete during cutover. I take extracts of every object in the wave. I restore parents first. I stop inbound integrations. I tell executives we cannot ask Salesforce to invent yesterday without a copy. I mention licensed Salesforce Backup only if the org has it.
interview_questions.example: Pre-load Account extract upserted back after a bad Status__c map.
tradeoffs: AllOrNone fail-closed vs partial success plus error file
weak_answer_warnings: One rollback story for every failure mode

interview_questions.question: Contact wave succeeds but AccountId is blank on many rows. Diagnose from the plan.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The parent key was unmapped, the Account upsert failed, or Contacts ran first. Check Account success counts and the Contact map for the Account External ID.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not start Opportunities. I open both error files. I verify LAB_ERP_Id__c on Account exists and was upserted. I check whether the Contact file used Salesforce Id instead of the External ID relationship. I fix the map and re-upsert Contacts only. I mention SOAP's parent-before-child array rule if they used a composite create.
interview_questions.example: Contact column Parent_ERP mapped to Account.Name, not the External ID relationship.
tradeoffs: Fix-forward upsert vs delete Contacts and reload
Wizard versus Loader for the child object
follow_ups: How do you relate without Salesforce Id?

interview_questions.question: A PM says Salesforce will roll the org back if we mess up the weekend load. Respond.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I ask which backup product and which restore drill we have. I explain Recycle Bin, Export Service, and Loader copies. I will not promise a platform Undo Migration. If we have no pre-image, I vote no-go.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I stay factual. Help tells customers to keep copies and restore from them. Sandboxes do not rewind production. AllOrNone already ended with each call. I offer a smaller wave, a freeze window, and a written rollback owner. I refuse hard delete. I document the decision.
interview_questions.example: Weekend Account overwrite with only a two-week-old weekly export and no extract last night—no-go.
tradeoffs: Smaller waves vs one big bang
follow_ups: Who pages if reconciliation fails at 2 a.m.?
weak_answer_warnings: Agreeing Salesforce will rewind the org

interview_questions.question: Teach the orchestra analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Plan is the program order, mapping is the score, rehearsal is the dress rehearsal, reconciliation is the take sheet, rollback is the archive—not an undo switch. It breaks because AllOrNone is one take, and a Developer hall may have no audience chairs.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map External IDs to union numbers that survive venues. I map metadata deploy to rebuilding the hall. I break it: no official Undo Concert; Export Service is a recording, not a time machine; LDV timeouts are a different topic. I avoid library and drawer language.
interview_questions.example: Teaching a PM why 20 chairs in a tiny hall do not prove a stadium show.
follow_ups: State Developer sandbox limits without the analogy.
State unmapped-field behavior without the analogy.
